source.title: Measuring and Guiding Monosemanticity
source.authors: Ruben Härle; Felix Friedrich; Manuel Brack; Stephan Wäldchen; Bjorn Deiseroth; P. Schramowski; K. Kersting

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Measures SAE feature representations in Llama3, applying monosemanticity and feature-distribution questions to an LLM setting rather than reproducing the original toy-model method.
record.gate_note: Rows record the unsupervised Vanilla SAE measurements on Llama3-8B-base. G-SAE results are not counted as evidence of naturally occurring feature representations because its training is explicitly conditioned on concept labels. Steering results do not measure the representation claim. The paper's statements about SAE feature instability and canonical units cite other work, so they are not recorded as study results.
record.test_reason: The study builds a metric (FMS) and applies it to unsupervised (vanilla) SAEs on Llama3-8B-base residual activations. It reports that SAE latents capture labelled concepts above chance but spread them over many latents, with near-zero isolation in any single latent. That bears on whether SAE features are clean, complete units (V5) and, more weakly, on whether SAEs recover concept features in LLMs (V4). The authors argue SAE features lack reliable monosemanticity, so this is a T5-type result rather than a mere T3 application.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right, with two corrections. The authors conclude current (vanilla) SAEs lack reliable monosemanticity, spreading concepts across many latents (FMS@1 ~0.27). Their supervised G-SAE enforces isolated concept latents, improving FMS, detection and steering without hurting SAE-Bench scores. The 'no guarantee concepts are present' point is mainly cited from Paulo & Belrose, though Fig. 10 shows it qualitatively for PII.
record.recipe_differences: This study measures and trains sparse autoencoders with a supervised concept-conditioning loss; it does not reproduce toy-model superposition experiments or measure overlapping near-orthogonal directions.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary by dataset/concept and by SAE training method; toxicity shows more modest monosemanticity improvement than privacy.

fits_no_version.finding: Supervised conditioning (G-SAE) places a labelled concept in an assigned latent, roughly doubling FMS (avg FMS@1 0.27 to 0.52). Its decoder rows also steer better.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Concept supervision during SAE training can enforce monosemantic latents without hurting SAE-Bench fidelity.

record.problems: Evidence on the claim is limited to SAE latent features from Llama3-8B-base and the selected labeled datasets. The paper's argument about feature instability/canonical units cites other work rather than measuring stability here. Table 1 provides no uncertainty values for its FMS entries, although standard deviations and statistical tests are reported elsewhere.
record.rows_left_out: Excluded G-SAE's label-conditioned FMS and detection results because those features are intentionally induced by supervised training, not evidence of naturally occurring unsupervised representations. Excluded cited findings and steering evaluations, which do not test the claim's representation geometry.

untested.parts: No toy models, sparsity transitions or geometry.
No test of capacity competition or dedicated dimensions for important features.
No test of non-capacity causes of polysemantic neurons; neurons themselves are not analysed.
No measure of feature spread over raw neurons. Only one model family is studied, with a task-specific SAE at blocks 3/11.
Stability across seeds/runs is not measured (cited from Paulo & Belrose only). Canonicity across SAE sizes is not measured (cited from Leask et al.).
No comparison of 1-D vs multi-dimensional features.

missing.what: Pretrained EleutherAI Llama-3-8B SAE (unsupervised, general data): accs0 0.75, FMSlocal@1 0.10, FMSglobal 0.79, FMS@1 0.34. Per-dataset values are in Table 8 (e.g. Privacy FMS@1 0.24, Toxicity FMSlocal@1 0.23).
Number of vanilla SAE latents needed to match the G-SAE root accuracy: 41 on average; IP 753, USERNAME/TEL several hundred; some concepts only 2-5.
Activation separation of the best vanilla latent: Mann-Whitney p<0.05, average RBC 0.18.
Vanilla SAE-Bench scores (absorption, sparse probing top-1 ~0.74-0.77, etc.).
Vanilla SAE accuracy after excluding top features converges only slowly to the random baseline, which the authors attribute to correlated latents.

record.verdict_notes: Most rows were relinked from V4 to V5. Low isolation of labelled concepts in SAE latents concerns SAE features as units, not whether models spread features over neurons. The record's V4 'supports' label reversed that logic. Caveats: the vanilla SAE is task-trained with sigmoid-TopK at ~9% density, which is atypically dense. FMS measures alignment with human-chosen concepts, and toxicity may be a composite concept. The 'baseline' for FMS rows should be the ideal score of 1 (or chance 0.5 for accs0), not G-SAE. Rows r19-r24 are aggregates of other rows.

versions.untested_parts: Toy networks, more sparse features than dimensions, sparsity-dependent transitions, overlap geometry, and near-orthogonality.
Does not test whether capacity competition causes neuron polysemanticity or whether important features receive dedicated dimensions.
Does not test alternative causes of polysemantic neurons independently of capacity pressure.
Tests SAE latent features on Llama3-8B-base and selected labeled concepts, not feature distribution across neurons in a range of LLMs or across all model representations.
Does not test whether SAE features are complete, stable across runs, or canonical units.
Does not compare one-dimensional feature directions with multidimensional features.

relation.reason: The study measures concept capacity and disentanglement in unsupervised vanilla SAEs, independently of its supervised G-SAE intervention.

tranche.reason: The vanilla-SAE measurements directly identify incomplete concept recovery and negligible single-feature isolation, qualifying V4 and challenging the monosemantic-unit component of V5.

source_check.notes: FMS has an ideal reference of 1, distinct from a measured baseline; local scores use the best remaining single-feature accuracy after exclusions. Conclusions concern labelled concepts and the tested SAE configurations, not an exhaustive inventory of model units.

reader_labels.condition: Unsupervised Vanilla SAE features on Llama3-8B-base across toxicity, Shakespeare, and privacy datasets
reader_labels.reason: Low Vanilla SAE local scores, including the average FMSlocal@1 of 0.02, support the finding that concepts are not isolated in one feature; the paper also says the Vanilla SAE needs 41 features on average to match G-SAE accuracy. Rows r3, r9, r15, r21, r4, r10, r16, r22.
